lines.text: This is the story of Riley Dare: Slightly Witchy Sleuth, by M.K. England.
An escape-room mystery with a flicker of magic.
Riley Dare loves puzzles and helps run her aunt's escape room, Level Up, adding a flicker of her own magic.

When a famous children's mystery author vanishes during a room themed on the town's biggest unsolved heist, and a ghost may have been spotted, Riley and her friends set out to link the disappearance to a crime from twelve years ago.
At its heart, this is a story about mystery, puzzles and friendship.
It's playful, curious and cozy: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
Pick it up if you love escape rooms and puzzles.
How does it end? Open Riley Dare on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of The Accidental Protector, by Amanda McKinney.
Romantic suspense at a remote security compound.
After a brutal attack, prosecutor Niki Avery goes into hiding at a remote security compound run by Gage Steele, a former Marine who never wanted to take over his late father's firm.
As questions about his father's death surface and danger finds Niki again, Gage has to decide how close he can let himself get to the woman he's protecting.
At its heart, this is a story about romance, suspense and protection.
It's romantic, tense and dramatic: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
Pick it up if you love romantic suspense.
How does it end? Open The Accidental Protector on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of God Save the Dork, by Sidin Vadukut.
Corporate comedy, now with jet lag.

Management consultant Robin 'Einstein' Varghese is sent to London to work on the Lederman account, and very little goes to plan: confusing pay, a colleague who sends mixed signals, museums that seem determined to defeat him, and a client threatening to pull the plug.
The second book in Sidin Vadukut's comic Dork trilogy.
At its heart, this is a story about office comedy, culture clash and ambition.
It's funny, light and satirical: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
Pick it up if you enjoy workplace comedy.
How does it end? Open God Save the Dork on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of What We Did to Survive, by Megan Lally.
A spring-break sail turns into a fight to survive.
Hannah is on spring break in Mexico with her best friend Emmy's family, including Emmy's older brother Jackson, her long-time crush.
When Emmy's wealthy new boyfriend charters a sailboat for their last day, theirs is the only boat leaving the marina as a storm rolls in, and the danger on board may be as deadly as the weather.
At its heart, this is a story about suspense, survival and secrets.
It's thrilling, tense and dark: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
Pick it up if you like fast young adult thrillers.
How does it end? Open What We Did to Survive on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of Nirmala & Normala, by Sowmya Rajendran.
A graphic-novel satire of film clichés.
Twins separated at birth grow up very differently: one becomes a film heroine, the other an ordinary woman.
Sowmya Rajendran's graphic novel, illustrated by Niveditha Subramaniam, uses the setup to skewer the clichés of commercial cinema and to call out the harassment that films often pass off as romance.
At its heart, this is a story about satire, cinema clichés and gender.
It's witty, sharp and playful: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
Pick it up if you love Indian cinema, and laughing at it.
How does it end? Open Nirmala & Normala on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of The Hidden Hindu, by Akshat Gupta.
Hindu mythology meets a modern thriller.
Twenty-one-year-old Prithvi is searching for Om Shastri, a mysterious aghori held and questioned at a high-tech facility on an isolated island.
Under hypnosis, Om claims to have lived through all four yugas and taken part in the Ramayana and the Mahabharata, and to be seeking the other immortals.
The first book in Akshat Gupta's trilogy.
At its heart, this is a story about mythology, immortality and mystery.
It's mind-bending, adventurous and epic: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
Pick it up if you love mythology retold as a thriller.
How does it end? Open The Hidden Hindu on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of Mumbai Confidential, by Saurav Mohapatra & Vivek Shinde.
Hard-boiled Mumbai noir in graphic-novel form.
Arjun Kadam was a rising star in Mumbai's encounter squad until the death of his wife sent him spiralling into depression and addiction.
A hit-and-run leaves him in a month-long coma, and what follows is a hard-boiled story of crime, punishment and redemption in the city's underbelly, told in graphic-novel form.
At its heart, this is a story about crime, city noir and redemption.
It's dark, gritty and intense: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
Pick it up if you like hard-boiled crime stories.
How does it end? Open Mumbai Confidential on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of Rich Dad Poor Dad, by Robert T. Kiyosaki.
Still the number one personal finance book of all time.
Twenty-five years on, Robert Kiyosaki's classic is still ranked the number one personal finance book of all time.
Contrasting the money lessons of his two father figures, it makes the case that financial literacy, not income, is what builds wealth, and this anniversary edition adds updates for today's world.
At its heart, this is a story about money mindset, financial literacy and entrepreneurship.
It's practical, motivating and accessible: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
Pick it up if you're new to personal finance.
How does it end? Open Rich Dad Poor Dad on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of Build an Epic Career, by Ankur Warikoo.
For everyone who is scared of settling for the wrong thing.
From the day we're born we're told to settle: finish college, find a job, get married, buy the house.
Ankur Warikoo speaks to readers who are scared of settling for the wrong thing, with a practical guide to building a career with money, growth, fulfilment and purpose.
At its heart, this is a story about career growth, self-reflection and purpose.
It's practical, motivating and modern: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
Pick it up if you're starting out or switching careers.
How does it end? Open Build an Epic Career on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of Atomic Habits, by James Clear.
Why tiny daily changes add up to big results.
Habits expert James Clear argues that lasting change doesn't come from one giant leap but from the compound effect of many small choices.
He explains how tiny routines grow into life-changing results, with practical tools such as habit stacking and the two-minute rule, backed by psychology and neuroscience.
At its heart, this is a story about habits, self-improvement and productivity.
It's practical, motivating and clear: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
Pick it up if you want a system, not just motivation.
How does it end? Open Atomic Habits on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of Ikigai, by Héctor García & Francesc Miralles.
The Japanese idea of a reason to get up in the morning.
Ikigai is the Japanese word for a reason to live: the point where your needs, passions, skills and sense of purpose meet.
The book explores how finding it is linked to a longer, happier life, and helps you work out what your own ikigai might be.
At its heart, this is a story about purpose, wellbeing and longevity.
It's calm, reflective and uplifting: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
Pick it up if you are looking for more meaning day to day.
How does it end? Open Ikigai on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of Heart Lamp, by Banu Mushtaq.
Stories of women’s everyday lives in southern India.
Translated from the Kannada, these stories capture the everyday lives of women and girls in Muslim communities in southern India, drawing on Banu Mushtaq's years as a journalist and lawyer.
They are witty, vivid and moving by turns, full of spirited children, bold grandmothers and mothers carrying more than anyone sees.
At its heart, this is a story about women’s lives, family & community and faith & power.
It's moving, witty and vivid: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
Pick it up if you love short stories.
How does it end? Open Heart Lamp on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of Can We Be Strangers Again?, by Shrijeet Shandilya.
Three college friends, one love story, and a betrayal.
Three college friends are bound by laughter, late-night talks and unspoken promises, until two of them fall in love and a betrayal breaks the group apart.
As friendships fracture and feelings get tangled, Dev has to decide whether he is willing to risk his heart all over again.
At its heart, this is a story about love, friendship and heartbreak.
It's romantic, emotional and bittersweet: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
Pick it up if you love college romances.
How does it end? Open Can We Be Strangers Again? on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of Mother Mary Comes to Me, by Arundhati Roy.
Arundhati Roy’s memoir of her mother, and of becoming a writer.

Shaken by the death of the mother she ran away from at eighteen, Arundhati Roy began this memoir: an intimate account of their relationship and of how she became the person and the writer she is, from the author of The God of Small Things.
At its heart, this is a story about mothers & daughters, memory and becoming a writer.
It's intimate, powerful and reflective: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
Pick it up if you loved The God of Small Things.
How does it end? Open Mother Mary Comes to Me on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of The Art of Letting Go, by Nick Trenton.
Quiet an overthinking mind and find your calm.
If your mind never switches off, this book is about clearing the clutter.
Nick Trenton offers psychology-based tips to stop dwelling on the past or worrying about a future that may never happen, manage your self-talk, and get back to a sense of inner peace.
At its heart, this is a story about overthinking, emotional calm and self-talk.
It's calming, practical and reassuring: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
Pick it up if you tend to overthink.
How does it end? Open The Art of Letting Go on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of Thank You for Leaving, by Rithvik Singh.
Poems for people who feel everything deeply.
A collection of poems for people who feel everything deeply: those who overthink, over-love and still believe in kindness.
Rithvik Singh writes about heartbreak, letting go and the privilege of feeling emotions intensely.
At its heart, this is a story about heartbreak, letting go and love.
It's tender, emotional and hopeful: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
Pick it up if you love modern poetry.
How does it end? Open Thank You for Leaving on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of The Housemaid, by Freida McFadden.
A live-in job that looks like a fresh start. It isn’t.
Desperate for a fresh start, Millie takes a live-in job cleaning the Winchesters’ beautiful home and looking after their daughter.
But Nina Winchester’s behaviour is strange, her husband seems more broken by the day, and the house is hiding more than it lets on.
At its heart, this is a story about suspense, secrets and twists.
It's thrilling, dark and addictive: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
Pick it up if you love twisty page-turners.
How does it end? Open The Housemaid on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of The Courage to Be Disliked, by Ichiro Kishimi & Fumitake Koga.
How to free yourself, change your life and find happiness.

Told as a conversation between a philosopher and a young man, this Japanese bestseller introduces the ideas of psychologist Alfred Adler: that we are not defined by our past, and that the courage to live freely, even at the risk of being disliked, is the path to real happiness.
At its heart, this is a story about freedom, happiness and relationships.
It's thought-provoking, calm and challenging: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
Pick it up if you like ideas explained through dialogue.
How does it end? Open The Courage to Be Disliked on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of 12 Rules for Life, by Jordan B. Peterson.
Twelve principles for a life of responsibility and meaning.
Clinical psychologist Jordan B.
Peterson draws on his practice and on lessons from humanity’s oldest myths and stories to offer twelve principles to live by, aimed at helping readers take responsibility and build a meaningful life.
At its heart, this is a story about responsibility, meaning and psychology.
It's direct, challenging and reflective: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
Pick it up if you want big-picture life principles.
How does it end? Open 12 Rules for Life on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of The Let Them Theory, by Mel Robbins.
Inspiring self-help.
Two words, “Let them”, to stop spending your energy on other people’s opinions and drama, and take back control of your own life.
It's inspiring: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
How does it end? Open The Let Them Theory on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of The Anxious Generation, by Jonathan Haidt.
Mind-bending and inspiring non-fiction.
How the shift from a play-based to a phone-based childhood between 2010 and 2015 rewired adolescence and fuelled a rise in teenage anxiety.
It's mind-bending and inspiring: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
How does it end? Open The Anxious Generation on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of It's Okay . . ., by Jaya Kishori.
Cozy and inspiring spirituality · self-help.
Spiritual speaker Jaya Kishori’s gentle reminder that everyone has problems, with advice for handling stress and living a more meaningful life.
It's cozy and inspiring: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
How does it end? Open It's Okay . . . on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of The Correspondent, by Virginia Evans.
Emotional and cozy literary fiction.
Told entirely in letters: Sybil Van Antwerp, a 73-year-old retired lawyer and keen gardener, writes to family, authors, neighbours and strangers about friendship, grief and second chances.
It's emotional and cozy: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
How does it end? Open The Correspondent on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of The Fourth Girl, by Arefa Tehsin.
Thrilling and dark mystery thriller.
Twenty years after a mysterious disappearance, three survivors are reunited at a funeral in Colombo, just as a journalist starts asking what happened to the fourth girl.
It's thrilling and dark: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
How does it end? Open The Fourth Girl on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of One of Us Is Lying, by Karen M. McManus.
Thrilling young adult thriller.
Simon, creator of Bayview High’s gossip app, dies the day before he can post his classmates’ secrets, and everyone who was in detention with him is a suspect.
It's thrilling: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
How does it end? Open One of Us Is Lying on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of The Inheritance Games, by Jennifer Lynn Barnes.
Adventurous and thrilling young adult mystery.
An eccentric billionaire leaves almost his entire fortune to Avery, a stranger.
To find out why, she moves into his mansion of puzzles and codes, and into a deadly game with his family.
It's adventurous and thrilling: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
How does it end? Open The Inheritance Games on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of The Vegetarian, by Han Kang.
Dark and mind-bending fiction in translation.
After recurring nightmares, Yeong-hye stops eating meat, and her quiet rebellion shocks her family and spirals into something stranger.
A disturbing, beautiful novel from the Nobel laureate.
It's dark and mind-bending: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
How does it end? Open The Vegetarian on Penguin, and find out.

title: At Night All Blood Is Black
author: David Diop

lines.text: This is the story of At Night All Blood Is Black, by David Diop.
Dark and emotional fiction in translation.
A Senegalese soldier fighting for France in the First World War loses his closest friend in the trenches and slides towards violence and madness.
International Booker Prize winner.
It's dark and emotional: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
How does it end? Open At Night All Blood Is Black on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of My First Sudha Murty Stories, by Sudha Murty.
Cozy children’s · ages 5+.
A full-colour treasury of Sudha Murty’s best-loved stories, full of magic, memorable characters and warmth, for children just discovering the joy of reading.
It's cozy: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
How does it end? Open My First Sudha Murty Stories on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of Wild Next Door, by Arefa Tehsin.
Adventurous children’s nature.
Grab a magnifying glass: a guide to the surprising creatures in your own home and garden, from hornets and termites to fireflies, skinks and a fish that seems to walk.
It's adventurous: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
How does it end? Open Wild Next Door on Penguin, and find out.
This is the story of The Naga Warriors 2, by Akshat Gupta.
Adventurous and dark mythological fiction.
The battle for Gokul: warrior sadhus stand against Ahmad Shah Abdali as Krishna, the mysterious Adhiraj and the nameless Naga face their fate.
From the author of The Hidden Hindu.
It's adventurous and dark: the kind of book that stays with you after the last page.
How does it end? Open The Naga Warriors 2 on Penguin, and find out.
